# Web3 Opportunities — grants for a Bitcoin project

_Bundled baseline as of 2026-08-24. Fields marked (*) are time-sensitive snapshots, not confirmed-today facts._

## Short answer: none of them, honestly

I ran the catalog rather than answering from memory, and the result is a clean zero:

- `--search bitcoin` → 0 results
- `--search btc` → 0 results
- `--search lightning` → 0 results

This isn't a gap in how I searched — it's structural. The catalog's chain facet only has these values: `ethereum`, `l2`, `solana`, `polkadot`, `cosmos`, `near`, `sui`, `multi-chain`. **Bitcoin isn't a taggable ecosystem in this dataset at all.** So there is no Spiral, no Brink, no OpenSats, no HRF Bitcoin Development Fund, no Stacks Foundation, no Bitcoin-L2 ecosystem program in here. Those exist in the real world; they are simply not in my roster, and I'd be making them up if I listed them with details.

## What the grant shelf actually holds

All 10 grants in the catalog, so you can see the shape of the gap:

| Grant | Chains | Status* |
|---|---|---|
| Ethereum Foundation ESP | ethereum, l2 | rolling* |
| Base ecosystem grants (Coinbase) | l2, ethereum | rolling* |
| Arbitrum Foundation Grants | l2, ethereum | rolling* |
| Optimism Grants (proactive) | l2, ethereum | closed* |

| Sui Foundation Grants | sui | open* |

Eight are hard-wired to a specific non-Bitcoin L1/L2. The two tagged `multi-chain` are the closest thing to a match, and I want to be careful not to oversell them:

- **Filecoin / Protocol Labs Grants** — non-dilutive, up to ~$50k, milestone-based, idea→MVP, global/remote. Open grants accepting, RFPs inactive.* https://github.com/filecoin-project/devgrants

`multi-chain` here means "the program isn't limited to one chain," not "the program funds Bitcoin work." Filecoin devgrants fund storage/IPFS-ecosystem work; Ronin grants fund things deployed on Ronin. A Bitcoin-native project only fits either one if you have a real Filecoin or Ronin surface — e.g. Bitcoin-anchored proofs of Filecoin storage. Don't apply just because the tag is permissive.

These aren't grants, but they're the routes in the catalog that don't care what chain you're on:

- **Gitcoin Grants & Bounties** (bounty, non-dilutive, any stage) — quadratic funding for open-source public goods. Now "Gitcoin 3.0," continuous model, next major round GG25.* Rounds are typically EVM-settled, but open-source Bitcoin tooling has historically been fundable as a public good. https://www.gitcoin.co/
- **DoraHacks** (hackathon + BUIDL grant platform, non-dilutive, idea→MVP) — continuously running ecosystem hackathons and quadratic grant rounds; the platform hosts whichever ecosystems sponsor a round.* This is the single most likely place in my roster for a Bitcoin-ecosystem round to show up. https://dorahacks.io/

So: the Builder profile is worth creating now regardless — it's reusable and round-independent — but before you write a round-specific application, confirm on grants.gitcoin.co that the window is actually open and note the closing date. Existing grantees usually get emailed at their registered address when a round opens; new applicants have to watch the channels above.

Also worth knowing: outside the flagship GG rounds, Gitcoin hosts **ecosystem and partner rounds** (a protocol or foundation funds a themed round on Gitcoin's infrastructure) and **continuous bounties**. Those have their own windows and often much less competition than a flagship round — check [explorer.gitcoin.co](https://explorer.gitcoin.co) for what's live at any moment.
